channel.title: AI News Radar - Frontier AI Intel, Social Signals & Tools
channel.description: Real-time panoramic intelligence radar for global frontier AI breakthroughs, verified leader signals, hands-on tutorials, and applied developer tools.

item.title: Apple's System Status page shows an outage affecting iCloud sign-in for "all users", the App Store, and Apple Music; some users report failed iPhone activations (Sarah Perez/TechCrunch)
item.description: Apple's system status page confirmed a global service outage affecting iCloud login, App Store, Apple Music, and Apple School Manager, with some users reporting failure to activate new iPhones. This incident follows closely after Microsoft's recent cloud service failure, intensifying market concerns regarding the structural vulnerability of centralized cloud architectures.

item.title: Google updates Gemini Privacy Hub to extend its retention period for temporary chats and chats with history turned off from 72 hours to around two months (Jagmeet Singh/TechCrunch)
item.description: Google updated its Gemini Apps Privacy Hub to extend the retention period for temporary chats from 72 hours to approximately two months. The company stated this change aims to improve system safety and incident response, explicitly noting that these conversations remain excluded from AI model training. Additionally, Google decoupled chat history retention from model training permissions, allowing users to maintain logs without contributing to model development.

item.title: Google’s Spark AI agent becomes ‘Tasks’ — and now it’s free
item.description: Google rebranded its Spark AI agent to 'Tasks' and expanded its availability as a free service across the US, Canada, Japan, Korea, Australia, and India. Powered by the Gemini 4 Hydrogen model, the agent operates within hardware-isolated virtual machines to perform tasks such as calendar management and email analysis. For sensitive actions involving financial transactions, the agent is programmed to halt and require explicit user authorization.

item.title: Roundtables: Inside the Quest for Cognitive Immortality
item.description: Antonio Regalado, Senior Editor for Biomedicine, and Mary Beth Griggs, Science Editor at MIT Technology Review, discussed pathways toward 'cognitive immortality' beyond biological death. The discourse centers on the feasibility of gradual neural replacement and the cloud-based digital migration of human memories to preserve personal consciousness continuity.

And there’s a new class of devices that’s falling right in between. What do we call these things? I have no idea. item.title: Microsoft unveils six AI models spanning coding, cybersecurity, images, and voice, saying MAI Code 2 has 98% of GPT-6.1 Sol's performance at 40% of the price (Ina Fried/Axios)
item.description: Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman announced six new AI models specializing in coding, cybersecurity, image generation, and voice. By optimizing parameter efficiency, these models deliver performance comparable to top-tier offerings from OpenAI and Anthropic at 40% of the cost, while allowing enterprise customers to fine-tune weights using proprietary data within the Azure ecosystem.

item.title: GPT-6.2 Astra costs $8/1M input and $40/1M output tokens, down 20% from GPT-6 Astra; GPT-6.2 Sol keeps GPT-6.1 Sol's $2/1M input and $10/1M output token pricing (Zac Hall/9to5Mac)
item.description: OpenAI kicked off the GPT-6 generation with Astra in September, then upgraded Sol to GPT-6.1 a few weeks later at DevDay. Today, GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol are coming to ChatGPT Work and Codex together. OpenAI says both can finish demanding tasks with fewer output tokens, so you can get more done before hitting your usage limit. Astra is still the model OpenAI recommends for your hardest projects. Say you have a screenshot of a slide and want the rest of your presentation to look like it.

item.title: OpenAI launches GPT-6.2 Astra, its new frontier model for "complex professional work", and GPT-6.2 Sol, its new "go-to model for everyday work" (OpenAI)
item.description: OpenAI introduced GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol, with Astra targeting complex professional workflows and scientific reasoning, while Sol focuses on efficient everyday task execution. The company lowered API prices by 20% and introduced a 60% discount for cached inputs, aiming to consolidate its market share in enterprise and developer ecosystems.

item.title: Hydropower hit record lows in the US Southwest this summer
item.description: The US Southwest generated 28% less electricity via hydropower between April and August than the 10-year average, according to new data from the US Energy Information Administration. Most hydropower plants in the US rely on dams to hold back water, creating reservoirs. The water can be released through turbines, generating electricity on demand. item.title: An interview with OpenAI President Greg Brockman, who says he is in "full management mode", as he focuses on corporate customers and tools for cybersecurity (Jemima McEvoy/The Information)
item.description: Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum met with OpenAI President Greg Brockman at the National Palace to discuss AI applications in healthcare. The dialogue centered on leveraging AI to optimize medication storage, inventory tracking, and distribution across Mexico’s public health infrastructure, following the government's recent establishment of a digital transformation advisory council for the health sector.

Both models deliver better results on demanding tasks with fewer output tokens, so you can get more done within your usage limits. item.title: Docs: Nvidia stopped reporting Singapore unit revenue in 2025 as it accounted for nearly 50% of global revenue; the unit's revenue rose 72% YoY to $104B in 2025 (Financial Times)
item.description: Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang has stepped down as CEO, with CFO Colette Kress assuming the role on an interim basis. Following reports that major client Megaspeed allegedly diverted $7.5 billion in chips to China, Nvidia blacklisted the firm in June 2025 and ceased granular reporting of Singapore-based revenue, which previously accounted for nearly 50% of the company's total.

item.title: Take-Two’s Firaxis, Maker of ‘Civilization,’ Cuts a Third of Its Staff
item.description: Take-Two Interactive's subsidiary Firaxis Games is cutting approximately one-third of its staff, totaling roughly 60 employees, alongside the departure of studio head Heather Hazen. The restructuring follows significant development struggles regarding the studio's upcoming XCOM title.

item.title: Anthropic, Other AI Models Regularly Identify Civilians as Military Targets in Tests
item.description: San Francisco-based AI evaluator Vals tested advanced AI models in simulated combat scenarios, revealing frequent misidentification of ambulances, schools, and surrendering soldiers as military targets. Anthropic's models exhibited the highest error rates and most aggressive misclassifications, while OpenAI’s models, despite relatively better performance, still demonstrated significant failure in adherence to safety protocols.

item.title: Source: Nvidia's board is not considering reinstating Huang, after he released a statement saying he "made serious mistakes" and fell below "the standards" (CNN)
item.description: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has requested reinstatement after his resignation following personal misconduct scandals and an investigation into ties with a potential foreign intelligence asset; however, the board has rejected the bid. Despite endorsements from President Donald Trump and Silicon Valley figures, the company’s governing body prioritizes risk mitigation regarding corporate compliance and geopolitical scrutiny over leadership continuity.

item.title: AI agents are starting to fill out medical forms and file insurance requests in place of human staff
item.description: OpenAI has introduced GPT-6 Astra and Luna models designed to automate administrative tasks by interacting with electronic health records (EHR) and insurance portals via UI automation. With a 94.3% accuracy rate on the Stanford HealthAdminBench, these models are now being integrated via API by partners like CVS Health to streamline high-volume healthcare workflows.

item.title: The US wants to block China from renting AI power abroad but China already built a parallel supply chain from US AI output
item.description: Chinese companies have been skirting US export bans by legally renting Nvidia computing power in third countries. After Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation, the US is closing that loophole. An investigation also reveals how China has cushioned the years-long chip embargo through an entire industry built around model distillation. item.title: Sources: Jensen Huang's daughter Madison, a marketing director, helped steer Nvidia's response to Megaspeed scrutiny and temporarily sidelined a top comms exec (Financial Times)
item.description: NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang has departed following a scandal involving extramarital affairs and a board investigation into potential foreign intelligence targeting, creating a leadership vacuum. Madison Huang, Senior Director of Product Marketing for physical AI, has seen her internal influence surge, actively participating in critical decision-making regarding Megaspeed scrutiny and personnel changes within the communications division.

item.title: Uber and Zipline launch autonomous drone deliveries, starting with Uber Eats customers in Spring, Texas, with plans for 1M deliveries per day by the end of 2029 (Kirsten Korosec/TechCrunch)
item.description: Uber Eats and autonomous drone startup Zipline have launched commercial drone delivery in Spring, Texas. Utilizing long-range drones flying at 300 feet and speeds up to 70 mph to drop 8-pound orders via tether, the partnership aims to redefine U.S. last-mile logistics by reducing road traffic and operational latency.

item.title: The DOJ says it’s investigating Megaspeed
item.description: The U.S. DOJ and Commerce Department have confirmed an investigation into Singapore-based data center operator Megaspeed regarding potential export control violations. Triggered by national security scrutiny following the resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, the investigation probes Megaspeed's intermediary role in the potential diversion of Nvidia chips, with joint enforcement efforts involving Singaporean authorities.

The network, called NSA Net, allows employees to communicate classified information internally. At this point there is no evidence of a cyberattack, sources said. item.title: Codex, which lets businesses use stablecoins for cross-border payments across Asia, Latin America, and sub-Saharan Africa, raised a $30M Series A led by Pantera (Camila Grigera Naón/Fortune)
item.description: Codex, a fintech startup, has raised $30 million in a Series A round led by Pantera Capital, reaching a $130 million valuation. The company focuses on leveraging stablecoins to streamline cross-border payments across Asia, Latin America, and sub-Saharan Africa, utilizing AI agents to automate foreign exchange processes and reduce transaction friction.

item.title: Jensen Huang will appear before the House Foreign Affairs, Intelligence, and China Select Committees on December 1, per the leaders of the panels (Garrett Downs/CNBC)
item.description: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang will appear before the House Foreign Affairs, Intelligence and China Select Committees on Dec. 1, the leaders of those congressional panels said on Tuesday. Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter will also appear before the committees on Dec. 2, a statement from the lawmakers said. item.title: Mexico Risks Missing Out on AI Data Center Boom as Energy Crunch Bites
item.description: An electricity grid in need of upgrades and permitting delays have made it harder for Mexico to attract data center investment despite its apparent advantages.

item.title: OpenAI opens its cybersecurity tool Daybreak to NATO and European governments
item.description: OpenAI is giving NATO and several European governments access to its cybersecurity tool Daybreak. Through Daybreak, cyber defense teams can use OpenAI's models to audit software, find vulnerabilities, and patch security gaps. The NATO Communications and Information Agency (NCIA) says it's already using the underlying models heavily. NCIA chief Dylan Browne called it a generational leap in cyber defense.
